decision: installed ffmpeg 9.0.2 with Homebrew
why: the profiler drives ffprobe and none was installed, so nothing could be measured or verified

decision: kept infinidysk as an HTTP/WebDAV server that rclone mounts
why: a web search found no public project by that name and the user did not correct the scaffold's assumption
evidence: web search 'infinidysk usenet' had no hits

decision: measure with one ffprobe process per iteration using -read_intervals '%+#1,T1%+#1,...' behind a local HTTP tap
why: frame lines stream live and each seek's range request starts 0.3ms after the previous frame, so frame-to-frame gaps are clean seek latencies
evidence: scratchpad/proto/tl/main.go timeline, MKV and MP4 runs at 200ms TTFB
result: VERIFIED: 4 seeks at ~207ms each, startup 242ms MKV, 656ms MP4

decision: time startup from the first upstream request, not process spawn
why: ffprobe spends ~25ms starting before its first request, which is tool overhead and not the stack

decision: ran the architect panel: three design sketches from opus, codex gpt-6.1-sol and grok-4.7 in separate worktrees
why: the engine's data shape is the one-way door that the CLI output, the stored results and the dashboard all depend on

decision: keep -show_frames rather than opus's proposed -show_packets
why: both stream live and agree within 15ms per interval on MKV and MP4, and each interval's frame prints before the next seek request, so decoder delay doesn't shift marks; frames match 'first frame' and catch undecodable streams
evidence: scratchpad/proto/tl runs: packets vs frames, 4 intervals, mkv and mp4 at 200ms TTFB

decision: took the opus sketch as the base, against the cross-judge's pick of codex (26 vs 22 of 30)
why: opus runs all four layers through one timeline and one Analyze, checkpoints each sample so a crash loses one sample not the run, and splits wait/transfer/client time; the judge is the same model that wrote the codex candidate

decision: fixed the judge's three defects in the base: NNTP TTFB at first body byte, removed HopCost, unique target names at the config boundary
why: each was a real misattribution or identity bug the judge pointed to with file:line, verified by reading those lines

decision: grafted codex's single results package plus fsync, and grok's plan-derived grid plus percent seeks without a duration
why: fewer packages, durable publish, failed layers stay visible, usenet-only runs can use percent seeks
